# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 2317
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/2317
- **Title**: fix(2311): scroll fast path never guesses - byte-exact k only, width-ambiguous rows repaint whole, belief self-heals
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/2311-tui-scroll-no-guess` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +440
- **Deletions**: -77
- **Created**: 2026-11-18T20:49:42Z
- **Updated**: 2026-11-19T04:15:51Z

## PR Description

Fixes #2311

## What broke
On repetitive transcripts (the money-session shape: N x `* edit: results/test_portfolio_sim.py`, footer counters changing every frame), `_detectScrollShift` picked a best-match k by **majority vote + 12.5% mismatch budget**. Several k values look plausible when rows repeat; the vote emitted a wrong `CSI S/T`, the physical screen mis-scrolled, and every later cell diff landed on false beliefs: 4 stale footers (63->69->95->119), digits fused into words (`414utopilot`), duplicated tokens. The `_lastGrid` belief never self-healed (only mode change/resize invalidated it), and the inline `insertAbove` branch never dropped it at all.

## Fix (all in `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/renderer.dart`)

**M1 - never guess.** The op fires only when **exactly one** candidate k (across both directions, k<=40) is eligible. The budget/majority gates remain but are cheapness-only: they decide whether the fast path pays off, never whether a k is trusted. Ambiguous => plain cell diff. (Pre-fix repro: periodic transcript with rewritten chrome rows — old detector emitted `CSI S 5` where the true shift was 2.)

**M2 - width-ambiguous rows repaint whole.** Rows whose cells carry `layoutUnstable` (#342 heuristic 2-cell widths: emoji-range clusters like ▸ ✓ ⏰) are **never trusted matches** in the scroll path — cell-equality says "unchanged" while wcwidth terminals lay the bytes out differently. They always ride the fully-enumerated repaint list and go through `_paintRow` (whole-row, terminal-laid-out), matching the surgical diff path's existing rule. The card's alternative (re-basing the width table to a terminal set) was rejected in favor of whole-row repaint, as the card prefers.

**Self-heal.** The #761 static-edge invariant (pinned contentful leading edge => no op) now reports its rejection; when it fires on the frame **right after** a scroll op, that op's shift belief is suspect — the renderer calls `invalidate()` and rebuilds the screen with one full repaint instead of diffing against the false grid forever.

**AC4 - external writes.** `CellRenderer.insertAbove`'s inline branch never cleared `_lastGrid` (the alt-screen branch did): the `writeln` scrolls the physical screen, so the next frame diffed against a stale belief. Both branches now invalidate. `WindowSizeMsg` resize, `clearScreen`, `scroll`, `release`, `setAltScreen` and the render-guard already invalidated — a grep-guard test pins them all against regression.

## Unchanged (REG guards)
- Non-repetitive true scrolls still emit the single cheap op (1 op + k fresh rows), in **both alt-screen and inline modes**.
- The identical-frame 0-byte skip is untouched.
- Enumerated live-chrome mismatches (spinner row) still ride the scroll fast path and are repainted.
- k>40 fallthrough kept: a 41-row shift takes the plain diff.

## Tests
`vendor/dart_tui/test/renderer_scroll_no_guess_test.dart` — 11 tests, TDD: AC1 ambiguity (periodic transcript where the old vote guessed k=5 vs true 2; repeated-rows+changing-footer shape) red pre-fix, green post-fix; AC2 enumerability + post-scroll self-heal; AC3 unstable-glyph overlap row (`⏰ tail` U+23F0) repaints whole even when cell-equal; AC4 behavioral inline-insertAbove + grep-guard; AC5 true-scroll REG both modes + k>40.

Validation (standalone Dart SDK in worktree): new file 11/11, full vendor suite **805 passing**, `dart analyze` clean on touched files (2 pre-existing findings in untouched `editor.dart`/`renderer_sync_test.dart`), `dart format` exact.

Note: `lib/src/cli/fa_tui*.dart` untouched (separate lane's PR). CI dispatch left to the owner's SM per fleet policy.

# Review Policy

Preset: `default` — resolved from: built-in default (resolution chain: projectConfig.reviewPolicy → workflow jobParams → built-in default).
Verification: `none` — findings post exactly as the review leg raised them — no second-stage verification.
Every verdict on this PR is traceable to this table.

| Severity | Round | Fix | Gates approval |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🚨 BLOCKING | rework | mandatory | YES |
| ⚠️ IMPORTANT | rework | mandatory | YES |
| 💡 SUGGESTION | polish | mandatory | no |
| 🪶 NIT | none | opportunistic | no |

# pr-2317: fix(2311): scroll fast path never guesses - byte-exact k only, width-ambiguous rows repaint whole, belief self-heals

## Description

Fixes #2311

## What broke
On repetitive transcripts (the money-session shape: N x `* edit: results/test_portfolio_sim.py`, footer counters changing every frame), `_detectScrollShift` picked a best-match k by **majority vote + 12.5% mismatch budget**. Several k values look plausible when rows repeat; the vote emitted a wrong `CSI S/T`, the physical screen mis-scrolled, and every later cell diff landed on false beliefs: 4 stale footers (63->69->95->119), digits fused into words (`414utopilot`), duplicated tokens. The `_lastGrid` belief never self-healed (only mode change/resize invalidated it), and the inline `insertAbove` branch never dropped it at all.

## Fix (all in `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/renderer.dart`)

**M1 - never guess.** The op fires only when **exactly one** candidate k (across both directions, k<=40) is eligible. The budget/majority gates remain but are cheapness-only: they decide whether the fast path pays off, never whether a k is trusted. Ambiguous => plain cell diff. (Pre-fix repro: periodic transcript with rewritten chrome rows — old detector emitted `CSI S 5` where the true shift was 2.)

**M2 - width-ambiguous rows repaint whole.** Rows whose cells carry `layoutUnstable` (#342 heuristic 2-cell widths: emoji-range clusters like ▸ ✓ ⏰) are **never trusted matches** in the scroll path — cell-equality says "unchanged" while wcwidth terminals lay the bytes out differently. They always ride the fully-enumerated repaint list and go through `_paintRow` (whole-row, terminal-laid-out), matching the surgical diff path's existing rule. The card's alternative (re-basing the width table to a terminal set) was rejected in favor of whole-row repaint, as the card prefers.

**Self-heal.** The #761 static-edge invariant (pinned contentful leading edge => no op) now reports its rejection; when it fires on the frame **right after** a scroll op, that op's shift belief is suspect — the renderer calls `invalidate()` and rebuilds the screen with one full repaint instead of diffing against the false grid forever.

**AC4 - external writes.** `CellRenderer.insertAbove`'s inline branch never cleared `_lastGrid` (the alt-screen branch did): the `writeln` scrolls the physical screen, so the next frame diffed against a stale belief. Both branches now invalidate. `WindowSizeMsg` resize, `clearScreen`, `scroll`, `release`, `setAltScreen` and the render-guard already invalidated — a grep-guard test pins them all against regression.

## Unchanged (REG guards)
- Non-repetitive true scrolls still emit the single cheap op (1 op + k fresh rows), in **both alt-screen and inline modes**.
- The identical-frame 0-byte skip is untouched.
- Enumerated live-chrome mismatches (spinner row) still ride the scroll fast path and are repainted.
- k>40 fallthrough kept: a 41-row shift takes the plain diff.

## Tests
`vendor/dart_tui/test/renderer_scroll_no_guess_test.dart` — 11 tests, TDD: AC1 ambiguity (periodic transcript where the old vote guessed k=5 vs true 2; repeated-rows+changing-footer shape) red pre-fix, green post-fix; AC2 enumerability + post-scroll self-heal; AC3 unstable-glyph overlap row (`⏰ tail` U+23F0) repaints whole even when cell-equal; AC4 behavioral inline-insertAbove + grep-guard; AC5 true-scroll REG both modes + k>40.

Validation (standalone Dart SDK in worktree): new file 11/11, full vendor suite **805 passing**, `dart analyze` clean on touched files (2 pre-existing findings in untouched `editor.dart`/`renderer_sync_test.dart`), `dart format` exact.

Note: `lib/src/cli/fa_tui*.dart` untouched (separate lane's PR). CI dispatch left to the owner's SM per fleet policy.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. This file is
the agent ENTRY document: the harness merges it into the system prompt with
a ~19 KB entry budget, so it must stay small enough to be fully visible.
Ceiling: **≤ 300 lines / ≤ 20 KB** — enforced by
`scripts/check_agents_md_size.sh` (pre-commit hook via `ci_fast_gate.sh` +
the CI `static` job). Subsystem essays live in `docs/` — index:
`docs/README.md`. Keep entries factual: paths, commands, invariants.

## Module map

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph CORE["SDK - flutter_agent_harness, pure Dart (lib/)"]
        AI["ai: providers, agent loop, sessions, compaction"]
        TOLS["tools: approval, redact, hashline, memory"]
        HOSTS["hosts: shared wiring, messaging, a2a, hub"]
    end
    subgraph PKG["packages/ - sibling Dart packages"]
        FAUI["fa_ui: widgets incl. trajectory"]
        DAP["dap_hub, fa_llm, fa_llm_mock"]
    end
    CLI["fa CLI - bin/ + lib/src/cli: TUI, slash commands, headless"]
    APP["Flutter app - flutter_app/: desktop, mobile, web shells"]
    EXT["Browser extension - browser_ext/ + lib/src/browser + serve_bridge"]
    OFFICE["Office add-in - office_addin/ + FA_HOST=office host"]
    GOLDEN["UI golden & styles - golden tests, themes, ui tests"]
    NETW["fa_network - external Go backend + network clients"]
    CORE --> CLI
    CORE --> APP
    CORE --> EXT
    PKG --> APP
    PKG --> CLI
    APP --> OFFICE
    CLI --> NETW
    APP --> NETW
    EXT --> NETW
    GOLDEN --> APP
    GOLDEN --> FAUI
```

## Project layout — one line per subsystem

Full subsystem reference: `docs/agents/sdk-subsystems.md` (SDK) +
`docs/agents/flutter-app-subsystems.md` (app/packages/repo-level).

**SDK core (`lib/`, pure Dart):**

- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers, session modes, per-tool overrides, critical-bash interceptor, per-turn grants.
- `lib/src/tools/` — `ask`/`request_secret`/media tools, `read` selectors + archives + sqlite, background shell jobs, availability + load modes.

## Hard architecture rules (stay inline)

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.
- Barrel `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart`: grouped **APPEND-ONLY** export
  sections — one `// ── <subsystem> ──` header per group, sorted by path
  within a group, new exports append to their group. No mini-barrels, no
  re-sorting (gh-1232).
- God-file ceiling: no `.dart` file over **2800** lines (crap4dart `loc`
  gate). Target < 2000 for primary files; split by concern into `part`
  files — never by extracting public API.

## Working in parallel (shared checkout + worktrees)

Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked; run no
heavy commands (full suites/analyze) in it; never `git stash` the user's
WIP; talk to peer agents through the messaging fabric, not their files.
Worktrees only if genuinely required — ask first, create detached under
`.worktrees/<name>/` from the remote tracking ref, remove when done.
Full policy: `docs/agents/parallel-worktrees.md`.

## Memory (footnote)

Before any non-trivial task, **search memory first** (`memory_search`,
then `memory_list` for fuzzy topics). Scopes: **project** = this repo
(`.fah/memory/note/` since gh-2185 — local-only, not committed; the
user's files: read freely, write only via `memory_add`), **user** = global/private. `memory_add` stores durable facts
only; supersede by delete + add — never leave solved problems to rot. The
host recomposes the `<memory>` prompt section after every add; tool wiring
is `memoryTools` + `lib/src/memory/`. Churn pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`;
usage details: `docs/agents/memory-usage.md`.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done: coverage first (`test/goldens/` + `golden_guard_test.dart`
map), real fonts (`ensureGoldenFonts`), full frames (1280x800 / 390x844),
determinism, eyes on pixels after `--update-goldens`, green
`flutter test test/goldens` + `scripts/check_goldens.py` (orphan snapshots
hard-fail). Full rules: `docs/agents/golden-tests.md`.

## Prompts live outside Dart code

Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (YAML frontmatter,
`{{token}}` placeholders) — never string literals in `.dart`. After
editing: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` regenerates the `.g.dart`
files (`test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` gates drift); Codex catalog
refresh: `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Details:
`docs/agents/prompts.md`.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The hook is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI classifies
PRs through the same script (`--dry-run`) — one classifier, one threshold
set, hook/CI parity via `GATE_STAGE` markers. Path rules: docs/markdown/
prompts-only → size + analyze; lib/bin/test/pubspec → +tests, coverage,
CRAP, dup, dupx; `test/integration/**` → +integration-mock;

and the Flutter app unless fundamentally impossible — then it MUST be in

- **Program survival (gh-1248):** an exception inside a `Cmd`, `update()`,
  or a mouse callback no longer stops the program. Those guards enqueued
  `InterruptMsg` — the program died while the embedding host kept running,
  and `Program.send` then silently dropped every later message: a live
  agent answering into a screen that never painted again (the
  dap_wake_hang flake family). Guards now log and keep running; under
  `withoutCatchPanics()` they rethrow — the flag means don't catch, so
  failures stay fatal and loud. Only
  `QuitMsg` and external cancellation end the program. (The render
  pipeline's own self-heal is gh-1197's `renderGuarded`.)

## 2.0.0 - 2026-08-08

This major release hardens the terminal runtime, ports the selected Bubble Tea
capabilities through P9, and removes the temporary compatibility APIs so the
package has one clear model, styling, and program-configuration path.

### Breaking changes

- **Models:** removed the `TeaModel` alias. Extend or implement `Model`
  directly.
- **Keys:** removed the `LegacyKeyMsg` alias. Use `KeyPressMsg` for press
  events or the shared `KeyMsg` base type.
- **Styles:** removed the raw ANSI `TuiStyle` helpers. Use immutable `Style`

💡 **SUGGESTION: sole-eligibility can be won by a single coincidental row at the k-tail (`overlap == 1`)**

At this gate a candidate with `overlap == rows - k == 1` needs only `trusted == 1` (`1 * 2 > 1`) and `mismatches == 0 <= budget` to become eligible — one blank-blank (or border-equal) row pair is enough for `k = rows - 1` to win **sole** eligibility and fire `CSI S rows-1`.

Verified repro against this branch (12-row grids, inline mode):

- Frame 1: rows `r0..r10` contentful, row 11 blank.
- Frame 2: full redraw — row 0 blank, rows `n1..n11` contentful, distinct.

Emitted: `\x1b[11S` + repaint of rows 2..12 — the redraw is misdetected as an 11-row scroll. The frame still **converges** (the fresh-tail repaint covers rows 2..12 and the blank edge is byte-faithful; a follow-up idle frame is silent), so this is not a belief-corruption bug — but the op ejects the previous screen's 11 contentful rows into terminal scrollback without any scroll having happened, which is exactly the #761 defect class this invariant exists to prevent. The blank-edge exemption ("a blank edge scrolls without a visible trace") only describes the edge row itself; at large k the *other* ejected rows are visible in scrollback as duplicated transcript content — the same user-visible family #231 reports.

Notes on severity: this shape is pre-existing (the old majority vote passed the same gates for `k = rows-1`, matched=1/overlap=1) and bounded (one spurious op per full-redraw frame with blank top+bottom edges — e.g. overlay/picker opens), so I classified it 💡 rather than ⚠️. A real-session repro showing duplicated transcript content in scrollback after an overlay open would raise it.

Suggested fix (one of):
- require `trusted >= 2` (or `overlap >= 2`) for eligibility — a one-row coincidence is not "byte-proof";
- or restrict the blank-edge exemption to small k (e.g. `k <= 4`), where "scrolls without a visible trace" actually holds.

💡 **SUGGESTION: hoist the per-row instability scan out of the k loop**

`_hasUnstableLayout(next[i])` and `_hasUnstableLayout(prev[i + k])` are re-evaluated for every `(k, i)` pair — up to `2 × maxK × rows` full row scans per detected frame (~80 scans of the same row on a full-height transcript). The old detector scanned each pair once with `_rowsEqual` only; this change adds the two instability scans on the same hot path, roughly doubling the probe cost on exactly the frames this fast path targets (live streaming transcripts).

Both terms depend only on the row index, not on k. Precompute once before the loop:

```dart
final unstableNext = [for (var i = 0; i < rows; i++) _hasUnstableLayout(next[i])];
final unstablePrev = [for (var i = 0; i < rows; i++) _hasUnstableLayout(prev[i])];
```

then index the arrays inside both direction loops (~40× fewer scans). Pure refactor, no behavior change. Not blocking — the big-O is unchanged and rows are terminal-bounded — but it is cheap to do while the loop is freshly rewritten.
